utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "lightly armed," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Sidearms or rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many had you seen?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Probably half a dozen. I can't be specific. Not very many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what a -- or do you have any understanding to a fixed military presence or fixed military position?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: A fixed military position, to my mind, is a position which is taken up on a more or less permanent basis to effect artillery or mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen a fixed military position in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No, none at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what trenches are?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen any trenches in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what bunkers are?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about bunkers? Had you seen any?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd seen no bunkers. Bunkers are reinforced emplacements, and I had seen none of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen any artillery in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from the time you received the letter, through the rest of the day, was there any perceptible change that accompanied General Strugar's taking over or replacing General Ruzinovski?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: For the rest of the day. Later that evening we were advised by the Croatian authorities that the front line had been moved forward around Cavtat by 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after receiving that news?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We contacted the JNA liaison officer, Captain Sofronije, who confirmed that it had indeed been moved forward, and the reason given was that there had been an attack on JNA soldiers at Gruda and one had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone captured or arrested?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: A number of Croatians had been captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion with regard to the meeting on the following date?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We asked to be able to meet with the liaison officer and also with Vice-Admiral Jokic on the following date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to the following date. October 14th, was a meeting held?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: At the same place as the previous meetings; just outside Cavtat, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on the borders of the airport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it held?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: It was held at lunchtime, about 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was present?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Ourselves, the ECM Monitoring Team, and the liaison officer, with his interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any conversation with the JNA personnel on that date?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we did, with the liaison officer, where we registered our complaint that we hadn't been informed of the attack which had caused the death of a JNA soldier before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, did you make any requests?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We asked that we be able to go to Gruda, to see the site and to see the people who had been allegedly arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they respond to your request?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: The liaison officer said that he would refer the matter to General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any other requests?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We asked for a meeting with General Strugar and also for him to meet with the representatives of the Dubrovnik Community in a similar manner to that which we had arranged with General Ruzinovski.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you want to meet with General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Because he was the new commanding general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the response to that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Then the liaison officer said that he would put this to the general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any other requests?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We made a number of requests in relation to the blockade and again the delivery of medical, et cetera, supplies to the community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other major requests made in addition to medical supplies?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, the major problem was, of course, the advancement of the front line, which we asked should be withdrawn to the position that it had been previously on the previous day, and that no patrols should be moved forward because this might aggravate the delicate situation that had arisen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did the JNA officers or the liaison officers respond to those requests of returning the front lines back to the older position or having no patrols stray beyond the front line?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, again, this matter -- these matters, they said, would have to be referred back to General Strugar, but General Strugar had in fact said that patrols would not go forward without his permission. Any patrols that would go forward would be only military police patrols, because there was no intention of occupying Cavtat or indeed Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion with regard to the repairs of the infrastructure?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. The general had agreed that these repairs should proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What general?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any further discussion that you had?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We would meet the following day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what time did the meeting end?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: The meeting ended, I suppose, about 4.00. I can't recall the precise time that the meeting ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before, just before the meeting ended, did the liaison officer have any other conversation that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I can't recall specifically at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know it's been a while, so -- about 12 years, sir. So let us look back to your diary. Did you, at the end of that day, write any notes in your diary in relation to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at your diary and see if that refreshes your recollection, sir. One moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 61, please. Just read that to yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. I do recall that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you also look at paragraph 60, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, could you tell us, having read those, what other conversation occurred on that date?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, this related to the request for the movement of refugees out of Dubrovnik to the north and south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what other conversation did -- or what statement did the liaison officer make before -- just before you had left or ended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: That all these matters were for General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a look at paragraph 61 again, sir.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. These were General Strugar's comments that were conveyed to us, saying that the people in command of the killers, of the JNA soldiers that had been attacked, were in Dubrovnik, that there the JNA's goodwill was being exploited. But again, he went on to say that they had to -- they still had a commitment in respect of Dubrovnik but the people of Dubrovnik -- our further discussion should be directed towards the evacuation of people from Dubrovnik to both north and south directions, which was something that we'd been told before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who conveyed this message to you on behalf of General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: The liaison officer, Captain Sofronije.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was -- what, if any, concerns did you have in relation to the evacuation of people?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Our concerns were to consider whether the evacuation of people from Dubrovnik was simply refugees being returned to their homes or whether, as the people in Dubrovnik feared, that the city was going to be taken over by JNA forces, and they wanted the civilians out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that the liaison officer had made some comment to you about the movement of refugees out of Dubrovnik to the north and south.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if any, concerns did you have at that time?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Our concerns were, you know, what this actually did mean; where were they going to go?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did you do after this conversation ended?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: After this conversation ended, we returned back to Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the next day, on the 15th, could you tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: On the 15th, there was a slight delay in going to Cavtat, but we went there again and met at the rendezvous point the JNA liaison officer, Captain Sofronije.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left, did you have anyone with you? Did you take anyone with you, first thing in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Before we got -- sorry, before we actually went to this meeting, we actually took the Croatian workers to Komolac to commence the repair of the electricity substation there. After that, we went straight back to Cavtat to meet with the liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these the repairs to the electrical system that had been discussed over the past several days?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the way to Cavtat, did you make any observations?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We saw that there were fresh troops in the area in new brown uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you got to the meeting place, who was present?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Present was the liaison officer, Captain Sofronije; and if I recall correctly, also Colonel Svicevic, but I'd have to refresh my memory, I think, on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that a little bit later, but did you meet with the liaison officer first?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any conversation with regard to your observations?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we did. And we were told that the change of uniforms simply indicated a handover of forces in the area, a change of units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other conversation did you have?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We were again asked that the front line not be -- be brought back and that no patrol go forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the response?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, the response was that the JNA felt that they had to consolidate their lines in view of the attacks that had been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they say whose decision it was in relation to front lines or patrols?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: The liaison officer confirmed that it was in fact General Strugar's responsibility and that patrols would only go forward on his instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any additional discussion that you had on that date?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I can't recall offhand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any decisions or any plans made for future meetings?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We had asked for -- again, for meetings with General Strugar so that the team that would be taking over from us on the following day would hopefully meet with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did that meeting end?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: At about 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We proceeded to return to our boat in Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened along the way?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: On the way towards Cavtat, after we passed through the front line, we observed a patrol of JNA soldiers carrying an anti-tank gun with them, proceeding towards Cavtat. We were briefly stopped. A little further on we heard a loudspeaker announcement, which effectively said to the citizens of Obod - which was the village just outside Cavtat - that they were to return to their homes immediately or Cavtat would be flattened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything else at that time?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We heard gunfire behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: We immediately went back to our boat. My Irish colleague stopped off en route in Cavtat to try and make contact through a field telephone system there. I, on getting back to the boat, arranged for a message to be got through to General Strugar via the coastal radio system, which operated from the boat, and this was our only means of communication with him, requesting that the patrol be withdrawn immediately and that an announcement -- a further announcement would be made withdrawing the original statement that Cavtat would be flattened if the residents didn't return to their -- to their houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether that message got through to the general at that time that it was made?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: At that time, it didn't get through. We were told that he was not available but the message would be passed to his headquarters for immediate attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the -- your other colleague who tried to send a message through Cavtat? Was he able to do anything?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Not as far as I'm aware, because at that time heavy machine-gun fire came across Cavtat, directed, I think, towards the church. But it went over our heads and over the boat at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, after -- lay flat on the ground to avoid the bullets. It stopped after a short period of time, and our colleague, Nolan, came back to the boat, having seen JNA forces enter Cavtat itself. We then immediately got into the boat, the shooting having stopped, and proceeded back to Cavtat -- back to Dubrovnik, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever receive a response from General Strugar, a response to the --

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- message that you had sent?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We received a telephone communication from him at about midnight or just after midnight that same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why had you contacted General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Because we believed that he had the authority to take action, as the commanding general of the forces in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he respond to your request?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: He responded by saying that he would send his liaison officer to check what had happened in respect of the loudspeaker announcements to the citizens at Obod and report back to us, but he also said that there had been attacks on JNA forces in the area from positions around Dubrovnik, and I believe these were attacks on naval vessels in the area, and that they would have to respond with all necessary force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I would like to show you a document that has an ERN number at the top 02191327. Would you look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, it's gone -- no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us how that document came to be prepared.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I wrote this down at the time the message was received by our interpreter at the Hotel Argentina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what exactly is this document?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: This is a transcript of the telephonic message from General Strugar to me on that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have any changes or alterations been made to your handwritten document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No, they haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this letter responsive to the request that you made?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is that so?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Because it indicates that he was aware of the allegation that we had made in respect of the threats to Cavtat. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to get this correct, you indicated that the interpreter read it to you and you wrote it down in English?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to offer this as Prosecution's Exhibit Number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be numbered Prosecution Exhibit P3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, after you completed this letter, what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I took it back to Zagreb with me, because later that morning we embarked again on the Slavija vessel to return to Zagreb, having been relieved by the succeeding team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you relieved after only approximately one week?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: It was the policy at that time that teams should only stay for about that period of time; in part, I think, because we had to take our own water, et cetera, with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what did you do with the letter once you got to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I handed that in to the tasking cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the evening of the 16th -- sorry, of the 15th and also of the 16th, did you continue to maintain a diary?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do with that diary when you got to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I handed it in as part of our report on our activities in Dubrovnik at the time, keeping a copy for myself as I had written it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to it after you handed it in?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it was filed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to look at a document which begins with page 02191294. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's in my handwriting and signed by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: This is part of the report that I made, part of my diary report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these your diary notes?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is included in this?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: This includes the names of all the individuals that took part in our negotiations, in our liaison meetings, and also details of what was discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "discussed," is that at the daily meetings?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: At the daily meetings that we had with the various sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this compiled when the information was fresh in your mind?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who else was involved in preparing this diary?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: My two colleagues, Mr. Zak and Mr. Nolan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you use to prepare the diary each day, or these notes each day?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Short notes that we had made at the meetings themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do with this document, report, diary, however you would like to refer to it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: This was handed in to the mission at Zagreb at the end of the -- when we got back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they do with it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: They filed it. I'm not sure whether any copies went to the Presidency of The Hague. Probably not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you maintain a copy?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to offer this at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be numbered Prosecution Exhibit P4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated you left Dubrovnik around October 16th. When did you return to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: On the -- we got back to Zagreb on the 18th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do or what assignments did you have when you returned to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I went back into the tasking cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as part of that tasking cell, what assignments did you have?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: My main assignments were making up reports for the ambassador, for the head of mission, and also for tasking other missions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the tasking cell, are they -- is that the group that receives the communications?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Basically, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the field.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you in that tasking cell?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: At that period, a week; until I returned to England.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during that week, did you receive any documents from the monitoring team?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the monitoring team in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you four documents and have you look at them. The first one would be 02191329.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recognise that as?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I recognise that as one of the reports that came from the team that relieved us at Dubrovnik. And my initial is, I think, at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to this document after you received it at the tasking cell?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: This would have been filed away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have any changes or alterations been made to it since the last time that you've seen this?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Not since I've seen this, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I would like to show him the four ones and then have them marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at this next letter, numbered 02191330. Would you look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise that. My signature is at the bottom of the page, again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: This again is another communication from the team that succeeded us in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, have any changes or alterations been made to this letter since you've last seen it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I ask you to look at the next letter, with the number 02191331.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the date of that letter, sir?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: The 20th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recognise that letter?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: I recognise it -- my signature, my initials are at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, it's another letter, another memorandum from the team that succeeded us in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have any changes or alterations been made to this letter since you've last seen it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, I ask you to look at the last letter, also dated October 20th, number 02191332. Would you look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, that is another letter coming from the team that succeeded us in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: And my initials are at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall receiving it while at the tasking unit, or the tasking cell?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we received that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have any changes or alterations been made to this letter since you've last seen it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to each of these four letters after they were received at the tasking cell?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, they were filed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could these four letters be marked for identification at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The four letters will be marked separately for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first document, numbered 02191329, Prosecution Exhibit P5; the second document, numbered 02191330, Prosecution Exhibit P6; the third document, numbered 02191331, Prosecution Exhibit P7; the fourth document, numbered 02191332, Prosecution Exhibit P8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have just had correction made with those four documents. Instead of being Exhibits P4 to P7, they will be marked for identification P4 to P7. Now, did you have something, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to say the same thing that you just remarked on. And, of course, the Defence will object to the authenticity of these documents, because they are obviously not written by the witness. When the time comes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic, yes. Although, correction has been made, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I add one thing? For the record, the documents will then be referred to as documents MFI5, MFI6, MFI7, and MFI8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when did you complete your tenure with the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that time, after you came back from Dubrovnik, did you have any other duties other than tasking cell?

utterances.speaker: ADRIEN STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you very much. Thank you, then. Now, do you wish to commence your cross-examination now, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the time being, I can only announce that the cross-examination of Mr. Stringer will last a little bit longer, and I don't know how purposeful it would be to begin now, because you have earlier announced a break and shorter working hours. I would not like our cross-examination to be interrupted, if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are of the view, Mr. Rodic, that in the present unusual circumstances, that it would be reasonable to adjourn now, with a view to cross-examination tomorrow, as you cannot finish in the time that is available now. It will not be our usual practice to do this, though, so I would advise both counsel that they should anticipate that they will run to the end of the session with cross-examination and it will then be interrupted and continue the next day. We don't want to lose too much time by this process. But in the special circumstances that exist at this moment, we will adjourn now to resume tomorrow at 2.15.
